about: Which runners take the heavy jobs: the pull request and main build fallbacks, the engine fallback and the nightly checks. Each of those jobs asks for this label beside thornswood-vps, so no more of them run at once than there are runners carrying it. Every other job on the box (board cards, dropped claims, the release jobs) still runs on any VPS runner. scripts/deploy/Set-BuildRunners.ps1 makes GitHub's runner labels match this file, and Install-Runner.ps1 registers a runner in this list with the label. Issue #2994.
label: thornswood-build
offBoxAbout: Off-box runners that take the pull request build's fallback too, by runner name (Install-Runner.ps1 -OffBox -Number n on One, the shipping PC). That job asks for this label alone, not thornswood-vps, because it needs nothing of the box; main's build stays on the box, which traces the gate (#3114, #3874), and every other heavy job and every box job still asks for thornswood-vps, which no off-box runner carries. One has its own cores, so they do not count against the box's cap. Patrick, 26 Oct 2026: build runners on One to clear the queue, "it's my PC". A name listed here with no runner registered under it is named and changes nothing. One runner only from 27 Oct 2026, 3:30 AM, until One's runners are on the Dev Drive (#4048): with all five building, Defender (MsMpEng) was One's biggest process at 2.7 to 3.2 cores while the disk sat at 2% busy, every file read ran 50 to 100 times slower than on the box (the secret scan 5 min 23 s against seconds), and whole-gate builds hit the 40-minute job limit (#3860). thornswood-pr-one-2 to -5 go back on this list in the change after the Dev Drive steps are done.
measured: 22 Oct 2026, after the gate went side by side (#3114, #3125, #3190): one build's gate now needs about 1,475 s of processor (PR #3190's build, 737 s on the clock with six at a time), so two builds fill the box's six cores by themselves. At four at once on 21 Oct the box sat 99.9% busy and each gate got what it could grab: #3106's build at 519b986 had 1,472 s of processor in 1,592 s, under one core, and 30 of its harnesses never started inside its 1,800 s, while #3190's beside it had 1,475 s in 737 s. A box that is busy either way cannot finish more builds an hour with four at once than with two; four only makes each one slower, past its time. With two, each gate has about three cores for its 1,475 s, near 8 minutes by that arithmetic (to be measured once it runs), and the others wait in GitHub's queue, which has no time limit. Before 22 Oct, when a gate ran one harness at a time: measured 21 Oct 2026 over the 558 box jobs that ran a harness step from 18 Oct to 04:30Z 21 Oct, a whole job took a median 18 min with 1 or 2 at once, 20.4 with 3, 21.7 with 4, 26.1 with 5, 31.7 with 6 and 36.2 with 7, and the box finished 3.4, 6.7, 8.8, 11.1, 11.5, 11.3 and 11.6 jobs an hour.
